$comment: Every model GLASSWALL runs, where its files must be placed, and what we have actually measured. A metric with status 'target' is an acceptance threshold, NOT a result: it stays 'target' until the gated suite named in `measured_by` runs against vendored weights and the number is written back here. Nothing in this file is fetched at runtime — see `install`.

models.name: Tiny 2-layer MLP
models.purpose: Inference spike fixture (P1-B). Not used in the pipeline.

models.name: Xenova/bert-base-NER (ONNX, int8)
models.purpose: P8 local NER. Advisory evidence for fusion; never authoritative for Tier 1.
models.license: MIT (model weights); the underlying bert-base-NER is Apache-2.0
models.trainingData: CoNLL-2003 English (Reuters newswire, 1996). Labels: PER, LOC, ORG, MISC.

install.note: Download once, commit under the path above. Transformers.js is pinned to this directory via env.localModelPath and env.allowRemoteModels=false; there is no CDN fallback and a missing file degrades to ner_unavailable, never to a network call.

alsoRequired.note: onnxruntime-web .wasm binaries, copied from node_modules/onnxruntime-web/dist. env.backends.onnx.wasm.wasmPaths points here; without it ORT fetches its runtime from jsdelivr.

knownGaps: Trained on 1996 Reuters newswire. Indian personal names are close to absent from CoNLL-2003, so recall on names like 'Priya Raghunathan' or 'Arjun Menon' is expected to sit well below the English-newswire figure. This is the single largest known weakness and belongs in MODEL_CARD.md verbatim.

No STREET_ADDRESS label. Addresses are inferred from LOC, which conflates a city, a country and a street. Recall on full Indian street addresses (house number + road + locality) is therefore structurally limited.
Latin script only. Devanagari, Tamil and Bengali names are not recognised at all.
Case-sensitive: all-caps or all-lowercase form fields degrade sharply.
Newswire register. Clinical and transactional prose (the ClinicDesk and MailLite surfaces) is out of domain.
mitigations: NER is one source among several. Fusion uses noisy-OR, so a missed entity can still be caught by a deterministic recognizer or by explain-or-redact coverage.
Anything NER cannot account for is unexplained and masked, so poor recall costs utility, not privacy.

models.name: Tesseract.js 5 (LSTM, English)
models.purpose: P9 targeted OCR on regions the DOM cannot explain. Never full-page.

install.note: Copy from node_modules/tesseract.js/dist, node_modules/tesseract.js-core and the tessdata release. All three of workerPath, corePath and langPath are set to these files; workerBlobURL is false (MV3 CSP blocks blob: workers) and cacheMethod is 'none' so it cannot decide to re-fetch language data. This is the single most likely way a CDN fetch gets into the repo.

metrics.name: box_error_px
metrics.note: Coordinate round trip is pure geometry and is measured without the engine.

knownGaps: WASM only. There is no WebGPU backend, so the WebGPU latency target does not apply to OCR.
Rotated, skewed or low-contrast text degrades sharply; watermarks are effectively unreadable.
English only. Devanagari and other scripts would need their own traineddata, which would roughly double the bundle.
mitigations: A crop that times out or cannot be read is reported unexplained and masked, so a bad read never produces a clean-looking region.
Budget of 6 crops per step at 512px; regions beyond the budget are masked rather than skipped.
